A.rationale: Strength: cleanly separates task vs job levels, confronts the neutral-vs-lagged puzzle as an evidence asymmetry, and explicitly rates its own confidence as medium while naming what future data would adjudicate. Weakness: a few key magnitudes (IMF 40/60) rest on a blog summary rather than the primary note, and an internal source label (S2) leaks into the prose.

B.rationale: Strength: rich, specific job-level evidence (Stanford, Indeed, Challenger) with the honest point that both purely-neutral and purely-lagged versions fail. Weakness: leans heavily on journalistic secondary coverage and forward-dated 2026 figures, and its handling of the macro-cycle confound is thinner than peers.

C.rationale: Strength: deploys genuinely contrary evidence (METR slowdown, Revelio heavy-adopters-hire-more) and a sophisticated Bessen-ATM mechanism-with-boundary, giving the strongest adversarial engagement of the three. Weakness: the front-loaded thesis is a dense near-conclusion and the cramped prose slightly strains the sub-questions-not-restatement ideal.

A.rationale: Strength: crisp time-varying thesis (supply-led surge, demand-led disinflation) that confronts the labor-market classification ambiguity and Storm's model critique head-on. Weakness: commits to fairly specific splits (2/3, 70%) that are more assertive than its own acknowledged wide uncertainty bands.

B.rationale: Strength: explicitly methodological, insisting attribution is only semi-quantitative, giving honest ranges, and steelmanning both schools' strongest arguments in a dedicated section. Weakness: several inputs (Furman, output gap, soft-landing confidence) come from secondary outlets rather than the primary sources.

C.rationale: Strength: the di Giovanni multiplicative-interaction point (6% not 9% without bottlenecks) and the euro-area contrast sharpen why single-side attribution oversimplifies. Weakness: reads more as a narrative synthesis and is slightly less methodologically self-critical than the strongest peer.

A.rationale: Strength: exceptionally clean three-channel decomposition with the sharp observation that baseline choice (vs fiscal vs no-intervention) can reverse the sign, plus the DFA counterfactual that asset booms are not share shifts. Weakness: an internal source label (S9) leaks into the text, a minor traceability slip.

B.rationale: Strength: the most concrete identification work, offering an LP-IV magnitude, high-frequency event studies to separate QE from slow structural trends, and a powerful deeper-recession-would-have-hurt-borrowers-more counterfactual. Weakness: little; at most the equalizing-employment evidence is asserted slightly faster than the asset-channel evidence.

C.rationale: Strength: unusually honest adversarial section that names the strongest counter to its own thesis and flags the IMF panel's own do-not-assess-unconventional disclaimer as a key evidence gap. Weakness: mis-maps its headline ~13% figure to the wrong reference (leaked S5 label), a real attribution error.

A.rationale: Strength: comprehensive, well-organized worse-vs-better ledger with a useful stock-risk-versus-flow-space asymmetry. Weakness: stays inside a conventional frame and never engages the meta-question of whether the Japan comparison is even valid, which its peers confront.

B.rationale: Strength: engages the Posen-vs-Pettis debate over whether the China-Japan analogy holds and is honest that female participation is falling, not rising. Weakness: sourcing is largely secondary/journalistic and a few hedging channels are asserted with thin magnitudes.

C.rationale: Strength: the sophisticated reframe that Japan's own world-leading automation failed to prevent stagnation, plus ICOR evidence that capital inefficiency predates the demographic shock. Weakness: relies mostly on secondary sources and a few cross-national figures gloss over definitional differences.

A.rationale: Strength: correctly frames near-zero as a bounded, threshold-dependent range result rather than a universal law, with strong calibration and graded policy implications. Weakness: thinnest sourcing of the set (four references), routing most quantified claims through a single Dube-Lindner survey rather than the identifiable primary studies.

B.rationale: Strength: cleanest mechanism-by-mechanism build on all-primary citations, with exemplary honesty that the negative estimates come from a contested camp and that aggregate job counts miss hours/quality margins. Weakness: little; the monopsony-limit and CBO framing could be tied more tightly to a single stated bite threshold.

C.rationale: Strength: substantively excellent, all-primary evidence (Hungary pass-through, automation margin) with a well-framed single-nonlinear-curve reconciliation and an honest hours/quality caveat. Weakness: the opening paragraph crams many studies into a dense data-dump, making the structure less layered than the strongest peer.
